item_name: Tokmakov et al. ICCV 2021 - Learning to Track with Object Permanence (PermaTrack)
depth_level: Short screening (as set in the item). Should not move to full analysis now: the mechanism (ConvGRU memory trained to hallucinate fully occluded objects) needs dense supervision of invisible objects, which the authors obtain only from synthetic Parallel Domain videos and which they show is ineffective below about 75 training videos; our BDD100K MOT labels are sparse (5 fps) and visible-only, so the recommendation would require a different training material (synthetic driving video with amodal labels). Kept as a source of explanation and of one cheap supervision rule (start supervising occluded objects only after 2 visible frames; constant-velocity pseudo-labels).
bibliography: Pavel Tokmakov, Jie Li, Wolfram Burgard, Adrien Gaidon. Learning to Track with Object Permanence. ICCV 2021; arXiv:2103.14258 (v1 26 Mar 2021, v2 30 Sep 2021 - same study, v2 is the ICCV version) [uncertain whether the arXiv v2 text is byte-identical to the ICCV proceedings]. PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2103.14258 ; code, models and data https://github.com/TRI-ML/permatrack (stated in the paper; not opened).
full_text_checked: Full arXiv main text read (sections 1-5, Tables 1-5). Appendix (dataset sizes of PD, nuScenes 3D results, joint-training details, MOT17 test) only partly present in the extracted text and not checked; code not opened.
task_and_output: Online joint detection and tracking (CenterTrack extended to arbitrary-length video): per frame, centre heatmap, size, offset, displacement for association, plus a new visibility head separating visible from fully occluded instances; outputs boxes of visible objects and maintains identities of occluded ones.
data_and_independent_videos: Synthetic Parallel Domain (PD) driving videos with labels for all objects incl. invisible ones, visibility fraction, 3D centres and camera matrices (number of videos in the appendix, not checked) [uncertain]; real: KITTI tracking (train/test), MOT17 (7 train videos; validation half split). Validation on PD removes invisible annotations for fair comparison.
target_size_and_input_resolution: CenterTrack/DLA backbone protocol (resolution as in CenterTrack; not restated in the main text) [uncertain]; ConvGRU feature dimension 256 with 7x7 kernels.
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: Car-mounted camera (PD, KITTI) with ego-motion; constant velocity pseudo-labels computed in 3D world coordinates because 2D constant velocity is not robust to camera motion; training clips of 17 frames (GPU memory limited); real data only as frame pairs.
detector_and_exemplar: Detector is part of the model (CenterPoint-style heads); no exemplar - identities propagated through the recurrent state and displacement vectors.
trainable_nodes_and_loss: Whole network end-to-end with backpropagation through time: focal loss on centre heatmap P and visibility map V, L1 on offset, size, displacement. Occluded objects supervised as positives for P and negatives for V only after being visible for 2 consecutive frames (thresholds T_vis 0.05, T_occl 0.15); invisible locations from 3D constant-velocity pseudo-ground-truth.
controls_seeds_splits: Table 1 architecture ablation vs CenterTrack (same PD data); Table 2 supervision strategies; Fig. 5 dataset-size curve; Table 3 domain adaptation (direct, fine-tune, joint; CenterTrack with the same joint recipe as control). Single runs; no seeds or intervals.
metrics_and_numbers: arXiv 2103.14258: Table 1 (PD val Track mAP): CenterTrack 60.3; pairs + ConvGRU 3x3 57.1; larger filter 59.6; no H_{t-1} 60.6; video training 62.4. Table 2: all invisible GT 62.2; filtered GT 65.9; 2D constant velocity 65.7; 3D constant velocity 67.0; CenterTrack + constant-velocity post-processing 61.2; ours + post-processing 67.9. Fig. 5: gap between invisible-supervised and visible-only model is close to 0 below 75 training videos. Table 3 (KITTI val Track mAP): CenterTrack 56.6; ours PD-only 60.8; fine-tuned 60.2 (Car AP drops 83.3 -> 75.7, i.e. forgetting); joint 70.5; CenterTrack joint 64.4. KITTI test (Table 4 text): +5 HOTA Car and +8.4 HOTA Person over CenterTrack. MOT17 val Table 5: IDF1 67.0/68.2 and MOTA 67.8/69.4 for two settings (public/private rows not separated in extraction) [uncertain].
tested_conditions: Unseen videos: yes (KITTI/MOT17 val/test). Target absence: partly - visibility head separates visible from occluded, but disappearance vs occlusion is not separately evaluated. Similar distractors: not reported. Occlusion: yes (central topic, but evaluated only on visible parts). Night/low light: not reported (motion blur mentioned qualitatively). Sequential operation on own predictions: yes (fully online, frame by frame).
mechanism_summary: Published: a spatial recurrent memory (ConvGRU over backbone feature maps) carries object evidence through full occlusion; a separate visibility head decides visible vs occluded; supervision for occluded objects starts only after 2 visible frames and uses 3D constant-velocity pseudo-locations; joint training with real frame pairs keeps the behaviour under domain shift. Proposed modification for us (not tested, not recommended now): a recurrent state on FlyVis output maps of a lost track, trained to keep the target location through occlusion with a separate 'occluded' output - this needs amodal labels we do not have.
transfer_limits: Needs dense labels of invisible objects; BDD100K MOT has visible-only labels at 5 fps (every 6th frame at 30 Hz) - the authors show that even KITTI-size data would be insufficient (Fig. 5) and that fine-tuning on visible-only real data unlearns the behaviour (Table 3). Requires deep RGB features with a large field of view (3x3 ConvGRU underperformed); our state is 34 cell types on 721 grey hexals in a moving, rescaling crop, so the memory would have to compensate crop motion. Learned hallucination only beats constant-velocity propagation by 5.8 mAP on synthetic data, and constant-velocity propagation is exactly what our Kalman prior already does; in the analysed R1 case the Kalman prior was right and the correction was wrong. FlyVis itself already has recurrent dynamics; a learned occlusion memory would be a new learned module over its outputs.
research_questions_addressed: 5.2 (memory through occlusion): design analogy and caution - memory helps only with large supervised synthetic data. 5.1: weak analogy - visibility head separates 'present but occluded' from 'visible'. 5.3, 5.4: not applicable directly.
candidate_node_change: Not applicable now (requires new training material). If ever revisited: node = state transfer of the fly readout for lost tracks; control without FlyVis = Kalman constant-velocity prior (the stand) and a ConvGRU on the eye input; stock FlyVis = same ConvGRU on C outputs; minimal check = on synthetic driving video with amodal labels only; stop condition = no gain over constant-velocity propagation on visible re-appearance.
strongest_objection: Its benefit over the classical constant-velocity heuristic exists only with large amodal synthetic supervision; with our data the honest baseline (Kalman prior) is already the published fallback, and the project's own failure case shows harm comes from overriding that prior, not from lacking a memory.
evidence_strength: Peer-reviewed ICCV 2021, code and data released (not opened), ablations single-run; the dataset-size and fine-tuning ablations are informative negative evidence for our setting. Moderate for the general claim, weak for transfer to FlyVis.
where_distinction_is_made: In a separate learned output (visibility head) on top of the recurrent memory: centre heatmap says 'object exists here', visibility map says 'visible vs fully occluded'; supervision filtering decides when an occluded object becomes a positive. Target outside area / insufficient data not separated.
feature_dependence: Depends on a deep RGB backbone with large receptive field; no evidence for small motion/brightness features.
association_consequence: Association by displacement vectors with greedy matching (CenterTrack); re-identification at dis-occlusion supervised by mapping the visible location to the hallucinated one. An external guard with a similar effect is the constant-velocity track propagation (Kalman prior; Track Rebirth in CenterTrack), which the paper shows gives part of the gain (+0.9 mAP on top of their model, and 61.2 vs 60.3 for CenterTrack).
difference_from_tried: Project tried observation memory and query memory (z13_observed_memory_v1, z13_query_memory_v1; main criterion not met) - memories of target observations for matching. PermaTrack differs by a learned spatial recurrent state supervised to predict occluded locations with amodal labels; no such supervision exists in the project, so the meaningful difference is the training material, not the readout.
memory_write_policy: ConvGRU state updated every frame with learned gates; no explicit check; occluded objects enter supervision only after 2 visible frames.
distractor_representation: Implicit (dense map memory of all objects); no explicit distractor buffer.
refusal_evidence_horizon: Accumulation over frames in the recurrent state; per-frame visibility decision.
loss_on_applied_decision: Partly - losses on centre/visibility maps and displacement used by the greedy association, not on final ID decisions.
association_entry_point: Track candidates and state update (hallucinated boxes keep the track alive; displacement links detections).
no_fly_control_equivalent: Kalman constant-velocity propagation of lost tracks (already in XYWHByteTrack) and Track Rebirth-style keeping of lost tracks for up to N frames.
hard_subset_evaluation: No hard subset; synthetic PD used to study occlusion.
temporal_information_availability: Only current and past frames (online, about 10 fps on V100); zero added latency.
